subject: Operational interlock: private VPC gateway + attachment design review
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@acmecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Feb 2028 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Operational interlock: private VPC gateway + attachment design review

Hi all —

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. Per follow-up from the call with Acme, attaching the latest sequence diagram and a short ops checklist. The two items we need sign-off on from Redwood side before we schedule the on-prem cutover are:

- Gateway attachment model: single shared edge gateway vs tenant-specific edge proxies. Tradeoffs attached in the diagram (v2).
- Observability & egress path: where will Acme's telemetry exit to our control plane and how do we annotate traces for tenant isolation.

Taylor — can you confirm whether Acme is comfortable with a routed /24 per attachment, or if BRIDGED L2 is still required for their legacy NAT solution? If bridged L2 is mandatory we need to adjust the ops checklist and provide VLAN tagging playbook.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) Redwood architects + Acme network to pick model by EOD Feb 3.
2) Ops readiness runbook finalized and shared Feb 4.
3) Schedule a test cutover window in the week of Feb 13.

Attachments: vpc-edge-gateway-seq-diagram-v2.pdf, ops-interlock-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Jonas
Principal Product Infra Eng
Redwood Inference

From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@acmecloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, NetEng Team <neteng@acmecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Feb 2028 11:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Operational interlock: private VPC gateway + attachment design review

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear summary. Short answers from Acme side:
- We prefer routed model if it preserves internal source IPs to our backend (we have legacy NAT configs but can adapt).
- Bridged L2 is still an option for a limited set of tenants that require MAC-level visibility; that would be treated as an exception.

To help decide, our neteng notes: if Redwood can advertise a /24 per attachment and provide a single egress NAT (with SNAT preserved), we can migrate most services without breaking monitoring. For the three legacy clusters we will need a temporary L2 bridge for 2–3 weeks.

We'll review the diagram and return with suggested VLAN ranges by EOD Feb 3.

—Taylor
Head of Network Engineering, Acme Cloud

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@acmecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 08:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Operational interlock: private VPC gateway + attachment design review

Jonas / Karthik —

Reviewed the seq diagram. A couple of questions and proposed clarifications for the ops checklist:

1) Health checks: we should add a control-plane-level liveness probe that verifies KV cache coherence after failover. Add line item in checklist: "post-failover kvcache sanity (tokenized checks)".
2) Telemetry routing: prefer that telemetry egress from the tenant cluster go to a dedicated telemetry collector in Acme's VPC over TLS on 443 (instead of outbound to our hosted control plane). That reduces cross-tenant visibility concerns.
3) For the L2 bridge exception flow: define explicit TTL for the temporary bridge (default 21 days) and an automatic alert to the account team when TTL hits 7 days.

If Acme can provide the VLAN ranges I will update the ops_interlock_checklist.xlsx and re-upload.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@acmecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 15:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Operational interlock: private VPC gateway + attachment design review

On Fri, Feb 3, 2028 at 8:42 AM Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com> wrote:
> Reviewed the seq diagram. A couple of questions and proposed clarifications for the ops checklist:
>
> 1) Health checks: we should add a control-plane-level liveness probe that verifies KV cache coherence after failover. Add line item in checklist: "post-failover kvcache sanity (tokenized checks)".
> 2) Telemetry routing: prefer that telemetry egress from the tenant cluster go to a dedicated telemetry collector in Acme's VPC over TLS on 443 (instead of outbound to our hosted control plane). That reduces cross-tenant visibility concerns.
> 3) For the L2 bridge exception flow: define explicit TTL for the temporary bridge (default 21 days) and an automatic alert to the account team when TTL hits 7 days.

All good notes — answering inline:
- KV cache probe: agreed. We'll add a kvcache-integrity check into the post-cutover smoke tests and expose a single boolean endpoint in ops runbook.
- Telemetry: Architecturally we can do collector-to-collector over TLS 443. Need to ensure the collector auth uses mTLS with client certs per-tenant. Ops action: generate client certs and rotate on a 30-day cadence (documented).
- L2 TTL: 21 days default OK. I'll add the 7-day alert hook to our escalation rules.

I'll push a small diagram overlay showing the collector egress path and the cert provisioning flow by EOD Feb 4.

Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Feb 2028 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Operational interlock: private VPC gateway + attachment design review

Thanks, team — this thread looks good and actionable. Summary / decisions so leadership can track:

- Model: Routed per-attachment (/24) as default. L2 bridge allowed as temporary exception for legacy clusters (TTL 21 days, 7-day alert).
- Observability: Telemetry -> Acme collector over TLS 443 with tenant-scoped mTLS certs.
- Ops: add post-failover kvcache sanity check and cert rotation procedure to runbook.
- Timeline: Acme to provide VLAN ranges and any special MAC requirements by EOD Feb 3 (Taylor). Ops runbook and diagram update by Redwood Feb 4 (Karthik/Neha). Test window week of Feb 13.

Jonas — please pull these into the top section of the ops-interlock-checklist.xlsx and share final with Acme once you have the VLAN ranges. If anything here looks wrong to the Acme team, flag immediately.

Marissa Cole
Director, Cloud Partnerships (on behalf of Deployments)
